public_rationale: He called Pichai's goal of 500 million Gemini users by the end of 2025 'so unrealistic' that Pichai should be fired. Google reported that the Gemini app had over 650 million monthly active users as of its Q3 2025 earnings on 2025-10-29, before the deadline. Court disclosures had already put it at 350 million in March 2025. Google later reported over 750 million. The target was not just reached but beaten, so the judgment that it was unrealistic did not hold. This grading treats his strong wording as an expectation that the goal would be missed. It does not treat it as a mere comment on odds.
limitations: 'Unrealistic' is wording about likelihood; the grade depends on reading it as a firm expectation of a miss.
Monthly-user counts are company-reported and not audited; definitions could include light use.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Gemini reaching 500 million users before the end of 2025 is unrealistic.

statement.excerpt: Sundar Pichai wants Gemini to be "used by 500 million people before the end of 2025," a number so unrealistic that someone at Google should have been fired, and that someone is Sundar Pichai.

from_speaker: Sundar Pichai wants Gemini to be "used by 500 million people before the end of 2025"
someone at Google should have been fired
our_interpretation: Calling the target 'so unrealistic' that the CEO should be fired is a strong judgment that Gemini would not get near 500 million users by end-2025. It is graded as such: reaching the target before the deadline contradicts the judgment.
Pichai's metric is taken as Google's own reported Gemini app monthly active users, the figure Google uses to track that goal.
The firing remark is opinion and is not scored.
criteria.support_condition: Google did not report 500 million or more Gemini users by 2025-12-31, and figures showed it falling well short.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Google reported 500 million or more Gemini users at any point before 2025-12-31.

evidence.explanation: Google reported more than 650 million monthly users two months before the deadline, well above the 500 million target he called unrealistic.
